content:
Last Friday (21st), during the sentencing of the Hong Kong Alliance case, police took away a woman who was queuing to observe the hearing in the early morning. In response to enquiries, the police said the woman was arrested on three charges, including "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed at a woman in the queue and said her "clothes were suspected of being somewhat seditious," before escorting her onto a police vehicle and leaving. While the officer took the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying they would "take them to the press area," and extended an orange cordon line towards Wah Ying Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they removed the cordon line. On the same day, a "court-watching" volunteer who was queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) enquired with the police about the reasons for the woman's removal and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation around the West Kowloon Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and is being detained for investigation.
